subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should `skills.entries.<skill>.env` itself count as the operator declaration that permits credential-shaped keys like `GOG_KEYRING_PASSWORD` to be injected for host `exec`, while still blocking dangerous host-control names?
rationale: The source-backed bug is clear, but the permanent rule changes which configured secrets can cross into subprocess execution, so automation should not decide the security boundary alone.

options.title: Allow configured host skill env keys
options.body: Treat explicit `skills.entries.<skill>.env` keys as allowed sensitive keys for host runs, keep the hard blocklist for host-control variables, and add focused tests/docs.

options.title: Require skill metadata declarations
options.body: Keep the current model where credential-shaped keys must be declared by skill metadata, then update `gog` or its package metadata to declare the headless keyring variables.

options.title: Keep secrets outside per-skill env
options.body: Close the direction by documenting top-level service env or SecretRef-only workflows, accepting that the current per-skill env documentation does not cover this use case.

recommendation.title: Allow configured host skill env keys
recommendation.body: Treat explicit `skills.entries.<skill>.env` keys as allowed sensitive keys for host runs, keep the hard blocklist for host-control variables, and add focused tests/docs.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is the best available owner signal for the original skill-env sanitizer boundary that must be adjusted or reaffirmed.
